rows.answer: {"answer":"The SEBI circular permitting intraday borrowing by mutual funds became effective on 1 September 2026. Mutual funds may avail intraday borrowing for (i) all unitholder payouts such as redemptions, IDCW payouts and interest, (ii) pay‑ins for investments made by the scheme, (iii) mark‑to‑market obligations and foreign‑exchange settlements, (iv) repayment of existing borrowings,
The intraday borrowing conditions apply from September 1, 2026.[3][1]
The cost of intraday borrowing is borne by the Asset Management Company (AMC) [1].

According to SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026, a mutual fund may not borrow more than twenty percent of the net assets of a scheme, and this rule is effective from 1 April 2026. An exception exists for intraday borrowing, which is not subject to the 20% limit, subject to conditions specified by the board. [4][4]
The risk‑ometer displays six risk levels – Low, Low to Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High and Very High – as defined in the Master Circular.[1][4]
The Large Cap Fund must invest at least 80% of its total assets in large‑cap stocks. [1]
The minimum number of investors required in an open‑ended scheme is 20 investors [1]. No single investor may hold more than 25 % of the scheme’s corpus [1].
The certification examination for mutual fund distributors is conducted by the National Institute of Securities Markets (NISM) (effective 1 April 2026) [1].
The Master Circular for Mutual Funds issued on 20 March 2026 (HO/24/13/11(1)2026‑IMD‑POD‑1/I/7602/2026) came into force on 1 April 2026 and replaced the earlier circular dated 27 June 2024 [1].

The Master Circular for Mutual Funds identified as SEBI/HO/IMD/DF2/CIR/P/2020/156, which was issued on 24 August 2020 and became effective on 24 August 2020, was the applicable master circular in January 2021.[1][2]

A Large Cap Fund must invest at least 80% of its total assets in large‑cap stocks.[2]

The July 10 2026 circular superseded the earlier guidelines on borrowings of mutual funds contained in clause 5.9.1 of the SEBI Master Circular for Mutual Funds dated 20 March 2026 and also replaced SEBI Circular HO/(92)2026‑IMD‑POD‑2/I/7885/2026 dated 25 March 2026.[4]
The Gazette Notification dated July 3 2026 amended the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026 to permit intraday borrowings by mutual funds for various purposes [1].
The SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026 (effective 1 April 2026) repealed and replaced the Securities & Exchange Board of India (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996[1].
The Master Circular issued on March 20 2026 replaces the earlier Master Circular for Mutual Funds dated June 27 2024. [1]
